chapter: Touring abroad and the future of music
title: Educators themselves, not organizations, advanced jazz education
summary: He believes jazz education was built by educators, not groups, and the new generation who played in school stage bands think clearly.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Nothing else. You share a lot of the ideals, of course, that I think Stan Kenton has expressed as well, in his own way.
Agonizing way, suffering the same things, of course, that fellows --

I've done what I do because it's the only thing I like to do, and I love it. So I have no axe to grind. But I don't approve of what they're into and the way they're suggesting that we go, generally speaking, because most of it has been all bullshit and --
You don't think they're helping, say, with --
Do you think the educational process has been helped in the last 25 years in jazz music, by any of those groupings? I don't. I think it's been done by the educators themselves.
I don't think that organization or the people that it stands for, if it stands --
Yeah, I don't think any of these organizations in any discipline actually help that much.

All I know is that the guys who have any kind of background at all, and now we have a whole new generation of guys, they have no background, they played in stage bands in high schools. And now they're the music educator. Which are guys comparable in age to my guys.
And their thinking is pretty clear. And I sit with them and I talk with them. I don't think they need any guidance other than their very own.
